content:
Your church needs an Employer Identification Number, or EIN, even if you have no employees. The IRS uses this nine-digit number to identify your organization for tax filing and reporting, and you can use it when opening a church bank account.

You can apply directly through the IRS for free. This guide walks through preparing the information, submitting an application, and keeping the confirmation. It covers the EIN process for a U.S. church.

---

## Know what the number does

An EIN identifies your organization. Receiving one does not establish its federal tax-exempt status. It is also different from a state sales-tax exemption number.

Keep the EIN application separate from questions about recognition of exemption. If you apply for IRS recognition, you need an EIN for that application, but the number itself says nothing about your church's tax status.

<Callout type="important">
IRS procedures and processing information in this guide were checked October 15, 2026. Before applying, confirm the current Form SS-4, instructions, online availability, fees, limits, and processing information with the IRS. The IRS currently charges no fee for an EIN.
</Callout>

---

## Form the church and check for an existing EIN

Wait until your organization is legally formed before applying. If you are creating a corporation, complete state formation first. Use the organization's legal name from its formation documents.

Before starting a new application, check whether your church already has an EIN. Look for the IRS assignment notice, check past tax returns, or ask the bank holding the church's account. If you still cannot find it, an authorized person can ask the IRS to recover the number after identity verification.

A single entity should have only one EIN. If you discover multiple numbers and do not know which to use, contact the IRS Business and Specialty Tax Line for help.

---

## Identify the responsible party

The IRS requires the name and taxpayer identification number of the responsible party. This is the person who ultimately controls the organization and its funds or assets. For a tax-exempt organization, it is generally the principal officer.

For a church, the responsible party must be a person, rather than another organization. Identify that person before filing. A nominee with only limited authority during formation cannot apply for the EIN or be listed as the responsible party.

If an authorized third party will apply, obtain the signed authorization the IRS requires. On a paper application, complete the Third Party Designee section and the signature area. That authorization ends when the IRS assigns and releases the EIN to the designee.

---

## Prepare your application information

Use Form SS-4, Application for Employer Identification Number, and its instructions to prepare. Gather the details before beginning the online session.

| Information | What to prepare |
|---|---|
| Legal and trade names | Legal name from the formation documents, plus a different trade name if applicable |
| Addresses | Mailing address and a different physical address if applicable; no P.O. box for the physical address |
| Responsible party | Full name and Social Security number or individual taxpayer identification number |
| Entity type | The church-specific option, called "Church or church-controlled organization" on Form SS-4 |
| Reason and dates | Reason for applying, starting date, and closing month of the accounting year |
| Activity and employees | Description of the church's activities and expected employee counts for the next 12 months |
| Previous application | Whether this same entity has already received an EIN |

For Form SS-4, select the church option on line 9a. The instructions reserve "Other nonprofit organization" for organizations other than churches or church-controlled organizations.

Answer the employment questions from your actual plans. If you expect no employees, enter zero in the employee-count boxes and skip line 14 as instructed. The IRS may use your answers to determine which federal tax returns you must file.

---

## Apply online through the IRS

The online tool is for domestic organizations formed in the United States or U.S. territories whose principal place of business is there. You must be the responsible party or an authorized representative and have the responsible party's SSN or ITIN.

- [ ] Open the IRS website's "Get an employer identification number" page and use its application button.
- [ ] Enter the church's information and answer the application questions.
- [ ] Submit the application in the same session.
- [ ] If approved, print the EIN confirmation letter for your records.

The IRS issues the number immediately online when it approves the application. The session cannot be saved for later and expires after 15 minutes of inactivity.

<Callout type="warning">
Use only one application method for the same entity. Do not send another application by fax or mail after applying online. The IRS limits EIN issuance to one per responsible party per day across all application methods.
</Callout>

---

## Use an alternative when needed

If you cannot apply online, complete Form SS-4 and use the IRS fax or mail instructions. Sign and date the application, and use the current destination for your location.

For a fax application, provide a return fax number. The SS-4 instructions say you can generally receive the EIN by fax within four business days. For mail, they say to complete the form at least four to five weeks before you need the number and expect it in approximately four weeks.

Treat those periods as estimates. The IRS warns that processing delays can occur. Telephone applications are available only to international applicants, so a domestic church should use the online, fax, or mail route.

---

## Save the confirmation and know when to use it

Print the online confirmation letter and keep a copy of Form SS-4 for your records. The online application also offers the option to save the assignment notice at the end of the session.

You can use your EIN immediately for most business needs, including opening a bank account. The IRS says to wait up to two weeks for electronic tax filing, electronic tax deposits or payments, and its Taxpayer Identification Number Matching Program.

<Callout type="tip">
If you need confirmation later, an authorized caller can request IRS Letter 147C, EIN Previously Assigned, through the Business and Specialty Tax Line. Recover or confirm the existing number rather than applying again because the original notice is missing.
</Callout>

---

## Keep the record current

Use Form 8822-B to report a change of address, location, or responsible party. Report a change of responsible party to the IRS within 60 days of the change.

You do not need a new EIN simply because your church changes its name, address, or responsible party. Changes in ownership or structure generally require a new number, so consult the IRS guidance when the entity itself changes.

Before submitting, check for these avoidable mistakes:

- [ ] Applying before legal formation is complete.
- [ ] Naming a formation nominee as the responsible party.
- [ ] Choosing the generic nonprofit category instead of the church category.
- [ ] Filing duplicate applications for the same entity.
- [ ] Treating an EIN confirmation as proof of tax exemption.

<Callout type="scripture">
*"But all things must be done properly and in an orderly manner."* — 1 Corinthians 14:40 (LSB)
</Callout>
excerpt: Prepare your church's EIN application, identify the responsible party, and keep the IRS confirmation without duplicating an existing number.
title: Getting Your Church's EIN

sources.claim: Opening and section 1: a church needs an EIN even without employees; identifies the organization.
sources.quote: Every organization must have an employer identification number (EIN), even if it will not have employees. The EIN is a unique number that identifies the organization to the Internal Revenue Service.

sources.claim: Opening: EIN has nine digits and is for tax filing and reporting.
sources.quote: An EIN is a 9-digit number (for example, 12-3456789) assigned to sole proprietors, corporations, partnerships, estates, trusts, and other entities for tax filing and reporting purposes.

sources.claim: Opening, important callout and section 5: direct IRS online application is free; answer and submit; immediate issuance is conditional on approval.
sources.quote: Use this tool to get an EIN directly from the IRS in minutes for free. Answer questions and submit the application. If it’s approved, we’ll issue your EIN immediately online.

sources.claim: Important callout: no IRS EIN fee; avoid paid lookalikes.
sources.quote: Beware of websites that charge for an EIN. You never have to pay a fee for an EIN.

sources.claim: Section 1 and final checklist: receiving an EIN does not establish tax-exempt status, and an EIN is needed to apply for recognition.
sources.quote: Applying for and receiving an EIN says nothing about the organization's tax status; however, your organization needs an EIN to apply for tax exemption.

sources.claim: Section 1: distinguish EIN from state sales-tax exemption number.
sources.quote: The EIN is not your tax-exempt number. That term generally refers to a number assigned by a state agency that identifies organizations as exempt from state sales and use taxes.

sources.claim: Section 2 and final checklist: form organization before applying.
sources.quote: Don't apply for an EIN until your organization is legally formed.

sources.claim: Section 2: state formation first for a corporation.
sources.quote: If you are creating a corporation or LLC, form your entity through the secretary of state before you apply for an EIN.

sources.claim: Section 2 and worksheet: legal name follows formation document.
sources.quote: Enter the legal name of the entity (or individual) applying for the EIN exactly as it appears on the social security card, charter, or other applicable legal document.

sources.claim: Sections 2 and 7: recover a lost number from notice, bank or prior returns; IRS identity verification for authorized caller.
sources.quote:
To find a missing EIN, try these steps:

Look for it on the notice we issued when you applied for an EIN
Contact the bank that has your business account
Check with agencies where you’ve applied for state or local licenses
Look on past business tax returns
If you still can’t find it, call us at 800-829-4933 Monday to Friday 7 a.m. - 7p.m. local time. Residents of Alaska and Hawaii should follow Pacific time. We’ll verify your identity and provide the number over the phone if you’re authorized to receive it.

sources.claim: Section 2: one EIN per entity; contact IRS when multiple EINs leave number uncertain.
sources.quote:
A business entity should have only one EIN.

If you have more than one EIN and aren’t sure which to use, call the Business and Specialty Tax Line at 800-829-4933 (TTY 800-829-4059) and we’ll tell you which number to use.

sources.claim: Section 3: responsible party controls entity and assets; supply name and taxpayer ID.
sources.quote: A responsible party is someone who owns, controls or exercises effective control over a business, nonprofit or other legal entity and directly or indirectly manages its funds and assets. When you apply for an employer identification number (EIN), you must name a qualified responsible party and submit their taxpayer ID number.

sources.claim: Section 3: generally principal officer for a tax-exempt organization.
sources.quote: For tax-exempt organizations, the responsible party is generally the same as the “principal officer” as defined in the Form 990 instructions.

sources.claim: Section 3: responsible party must be individual for church.
sources.quote: Your responsible party must be a person, not an entity. The only exception is for government entities.

sources.claim: Section 3 and final checklist: nominee cannot apply or be listed; identify responsible party first.
sources.quote:
A nominee is someone you give limited authority to act for your entity during its formation. The nominee has little or no control over the entity's assets.

Nominees can’t apply for an EIN and shouldn’t be listed on Form SS-4.

If you haven’t identified a responsible party yet and use a nominee to process your entity’s state formation, you must identify the responsible party before you apply for an EIN.

sources.claim: Section 3: third party needs signed authorization.
sources.quote: If you’re a third-party designee, you must have signed authorization to apply.

sources.claim: Section 3: paper designee authorization, scope and termination.
sources.quote: Complete this section only if you want to authorize the named individual to answer questions about the completion of Form SS-4 and receive the entity’s newly assigned EIN. You must complete the signature area for the authorization to be valid. The designee’s authority terminates at the time the EIN is assigned and released to the designee.

sources.claim: Section 4: Form SS-4 and instructions used to prepare EIN application.
sources.quote: Use these instructions to complete Form SS-4, Application for Employer Identification Number (EIN).

sources.claim: Worksheet: distinct trade name.
sources.quote: Enter the trade name of the business if different from the legal name. The trade name is the “doing business as” (DBA) name.

sources.claim: Worksheet: mailing address for correspondence.
sources.quote: Enter the mailing address for the entity's correspondence.

sources.claim: Worksheet: physical address distinct from mailing; no PO box.
sources.quote: Provide the entity’s physical address only if different from its mailing address shown on lines 4a–4b. Don’t enter a P.O. box number here.

sources.claim: Worksheet: full name and personal taxpayer ID of responsible party.
sources.quote: List the name and taxpayer ID number (Social Security number or individual tax ID number) of your responsible party.

sources.claim: Worksheet, section 4 and final checklist: church-specific option on line 9a.
sources.quote:
9a Type of entity (check only one box). Caution: If 8a is “Yes,” see the instructions for the correct box to check.
Sole proprietor (SSN) Estate (SSN of decedent)
Partnership Plan administrator (TIN)
Corporation (enter form number to be filed) Trust (TIN of grantor)
Personal service corporation Military/National Guard State/local government
Church or church-controlled organization Farmers’ cooperative Federal government

sources.claim: Section 4: other nonprofit category excludes churches.
sources.quote: Check the Other nonprofit organization box if the nonprofit organization is other than a church or church-controlled organization and specify the type of nonprofit organization (for example, an educational organization).

sources.claim: Worksheet: reason for applying.
sources.quote: 10 Reason for applying (check only one box)

sources.claim: Worksheet: starting date.
sources.quote: 11 Date business started or acquired (month, day, year). See instructions.

sources.claim: Worksheet: closing month of the accounting year.
sources.quote: 12 Closing month of accounting year

sources.claim: Worksheet and section 4: 12-month employee counts, include zero, skip line 14 if none expected.
sources.quote:
Complete each box by entering the number (including zero (-0-)) of Agricultural, Household, or Other employees expected by the applicant in the next 12 months.

If no employees are expected, skip line 14.

sources.claim: Worksheet: describe principal activity in application.
sources.quote: Use line 17 to describe the applicant’s principal line of business in more detail. An entry is required.

sources.claim: Worksheet: check whether same entity previously received EIN.
sources.quote: Check the applicable box to indicate whether or not the applicant entity applying for an EIN was issued one previously.

sources.claim: Section 4: answers affect federal return requirements.
sources.quote: Information on this form may be used to determine which federal tax returns you’re required to file and to provide you with related forms and publications.

sources.claim: Section 5: online eligibility, representative and SSN or ITIN.
sources.quote:
You are a domestic organization, formed or created in the United States or U.S. territories.
Your principal place of business is in the U.S. or U.S. territories.
You're the responsible party in control of the entity or its authorized representative.
You have the responsible party’s Social Security number (SSN) or individual taxpayer ID number (ITIN).

sources.claim: Section 5 checklist, preparation and section 7: single session, inactivity expiry and print notice.
sources.quote:
Complete the application in one session. You can't save it for later.
It expires after 15 minutes of inactivity, and you’ll need to start over.
Print your EIN confirmation letter for your records.

sources.claim: Section 5 warning and final checklist: one application method per entity.
sources.quote: Use only one method for each entity so you don’t receive more than one EIN for an entity.

sources.claim: Section 5 warning: daily limit is per responsible party and applies to all methods.
sources.quote: To ensure fair and equitable treatment for all taxpayers, EIN issuances are limited to one per responsible party, per day. For trusts, the limitation is applied to the grantor, owner, or trustor. For estates, the limitation is applied to the decedent (decedent estate) or the debtor (bankruptcy estate). This limitation is applicable to all requests for EINs whether online, telephone, fax, or mail.

sources.claim: Section 6: fax processing estimate.
sources.quote: Under the Fax-TIN program, you can receive your EIN by fax generally within 4 business days. Complete and fax Form SS-4 to the IRS using the appropriate fax number below.

sources.claim: Section 6: give return fax number.
sources.quote: Be sure to provide your fax number so the IRS can fax the EIN back to you.

sources.claim: Section 6: signed mail application; lead time and location-specific destination.
sources.quote: Complete Form SS-4 at least 4 to 5 weeks before you will need an EIN. Sign and date the application and mail it to the appropriate address.

sources.claim: Section 6: mail processing estimate.
sources.quote: You will receive your EIN in the mail in approximately 4 weeks.

sources.claim: Section 6 and important callout: processing estimates can change and delays occur.
sources.quote: High inventory levels may result in processing delays.

sources.claim: Section 6: domestic applicants cannot receive EIN by telephone.
sources.quote: The IRS no longer issues EINs by telephone for domestic taxpayers. Only international applicants can receive an EIN by telephone.

sources.claim: Section 6: signature required for corporation/unincorporated organization.
sources.quote: When required, the application must be signed by (a) the individual, if the applicant is an individual; (b) the president, vice president, or other principal officer, if the applicant is a corporation; (c) a responsible and duly authorized member or officer having knowledge of its affairs, if the applicant is a partnership, government entity, or other unincorporated organization; or (d) the fiduciary, if the applicant is a trust or an estate.

sources.claim: Section 7: keep Form SS-4 copy.
sources.quote: See separate instructions for each line. Keep a copy for your records.

sources.claim: Section 7: view, print and save notice at end of online session.
sources.quote: Taxpayers who apply online have an option to view, print, and save their EIN assignment notice at the end of the session.

sources.claim: Opening and section 7: immediate bank use, with up to two weeks for specified electronic services.
sources.quote:
You can use your EIN immediately for most business needs. For example, when you:

Open a bank account
Apply for business licenses
File a tax return by mail

Wait up to 2 weeks to:
Pass an IRS Taxpayer ID Number (TIN) Matching Program
E-file a tax return
Make tax deposits and pay electronically

sources.claim: Section 7 tip: request Letter 147C for confirmation.
sources.quote: Call our business and specialty tax line. Request Letter 147C, EIN Previously Assigned.

sources.claim: Section 8: Form 8822-B for address/location/party; 60-day deadline for responsible-party change.
sources.quote: Use Form 8822-B to report changes to your responsible party, address or location. Changes in responsible parties must be reported to the IRS within 60 days.

sources.claim: Section 8: distinguish new EIN trigger from name/address/party changes.
sources.quote:
You need a new EIN, in general, when you change your entity’s ownership or structure.

You don’t need a new EIN to change your business name, address or responsible party.

sources.claim: Scripture: 1 Corinthians 14:40 LSB, one verse opened individually.
sources.publisher: The Lockman Foundation / Three Sixteen Publishing
sources.quote: But all things must be done properly and in an orderly manner.

claim_check.notes: Author source mapping is ready for independent Opus review; source quotations are evidence, not a passed claim check. Volatile IRS application requirements, no-fee policy, daily/session limits, processing estimates and update deadline checked 2026-10-15.

rulings: 2026-10-15: Inherit phase 0 from the Legal section because backlog A1 has no phase; normalize backlog how-to to seed content_type how_to.

2026-10-15: Scope is a U.S. church EIN application; exclude recognition-of-exemption, payroll, state-exemption and banking procedures. Use church-specific Form SS-4 line 9a option, not Other nonprofit organization.

2026-10-15: Omit exact service hours, phone/fax destinations and mailing addresses; direct readers to current IRS instructions. Keep source processing qualifiers and the 60-day deadline specific to responsible-party changes.
